**Verdict: clean. No blockers.** This is the independent safety-floor review. It builds on Windows; the earlier marker comment ran on macOS.

**What this review ran (worktree head e7d49a2a5, merged clean with origin/main a277dd9d5):**
- `cargo test -j 6 -p camcraft-tools -- --test-threads=6`: lib 84 pass, 0 fail; all integration binaries pass. The four new `holder_library::weldon::tests` pass by name.
- Touched app binaries: `holder_library` 12 pass (with `a_weldon_pick_takes_the_bore_of_the_tools_shank`), `mcp_holder` 5 pass, `tool_body` 12 pass, `tool_body_bands` 13 pass; app lib 340 pass, 0 fail.
- `cargo test -j 6 -p camcraft-ui --lib tool_holder -- --test-threads=6`: 6 pass. The new `one_weldon_row_for_each_taper_takes_the_bore_of_the_shank` and the updated TTS list test pass.
- `cargo clippy -j 6 -p camcraft-tools -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

**Collision-envelope verdict.** A grouped pick cannot change a holder envelope. `weldon_for` (crates/tools/src/holder_library_weldon.rs:65-75) returns a copy of the library's own per-bore `HolderEntry`. No path draws an envelope from the grouped name. The fit uses `fits_shank` (crates/tools/src/holder_library.rs:220-229): the shank must lie within 0.02 mm (`BORE_SLACK`) of a bore; no two bores of a taper are closer than 0.35 mm, so at most one bore matches; a NaN or infinite shank fails the match and is refused. `library_body` (crates/app/src/commands/tool_body.rs:79-82) resolves at command creation, fit-checks again, and refuses by name before any body lands. `AddTool` records the resolved per-bore name (crates/app/src/commands/tool.rs:127), so project files and `holder_lookup` never see a grouped name. A Weldon-picked tool therefore carries exactly the chosen bore entry's outline, body diameter and collision bands: it cannot pass a check that the enlarged holder envelope should fail. The bands are pinned band for band for every bore of every taper (crates/tools/src/holder_library_weldon_tests.rs:76-87), and the command test pins the drawn outline, the judged holder and the bands against the old entry.

**Law checks.**
- The picker lands through the undoable `SetToolBody::library` command (crates/ui/src/state_tool_profile.rs:223, 230). No direct field write on a tool.
- No `unwrap` or `expect` outside tests on added lines; the one added `unwrap_or` cannot panic.
- No Cargo.toml change, so no new dependency edge; `docs/decisions/2018-weldon-per-taper.md` records the design.
- No snapshot PNG in the diff. The body carries the Changelog line. The commits follow Conventional Commits.
- MCP: `set_tool_holder` routes to the same command (crates/app/src/mcp/holders.rs:85); no new command, so no new tool or follow-up is owed. The schema text names the grouped pick.

**Note (not blocking).** A machine `.mch` `tooling.default_holder` still takes only a per-bore name, through `holder_lookup` (crates/app/src/machine/holders.rs:13), as the PR body states.

**Verdict: clean; no change requested.**

Built and tested locally: camcraft-tools lib 84 tests, camcraft-app holder/tool/body suites, camcraft-ui tool_holder filter, clippy -D warnings clean, all at -j 6. Safety-floor conclusion: a grouped Weldon pick cannot change a collision envelope.
